key_insight: LLaMat — a family of LLMs continued-pretrained on materials science text — shows that smaller, specialized models can outperform larger general-purpose LLMs; notably, highly pretrained LLaMA-3 adapts less effectively to a new scientific domain than LLaMA-2.
problem_solved: Addresses the gap where large general LLMs underperform on specialized scientific tasks and where naively scaling size is costly; provides strategies to build cost-efficient, high-performing domain models and explains how continued pretraining affects adaptability.
method: Create the LLaMat family by continued pretraining LLaMA checkpoints on curated materials-science corpora.
Benchmark LLaMat variants against larger general LLMs across materials-science tasks to compare performance vs. model size.
Analyze adaptation dynamics and show that extensive pretraining (LLaMA-3) can reduce flexibility for domain transfer relative to less-extensively pretrained models (LLaMA-2).
impact: Guides AI/ML practitioners to prefer targeted continued pretraining over brute-force scaling for domain-specific applications, lowering compute and data costs while improving task performance; provides practical insights into transferability trade-offs between model families.
visual_elements: Line/bar chart: task performance vs. model size showing smaller LLaMat models outperforming larger general LLMs.
Pipeline diagram: source corpus → continued pretraining → LLaMat family → downstream evaluation.
Side-by-side comparison heatmap: adaptation gains for LLaMA-2 vs LLaMA-3 across materials tasks.
Icon infographic: compute/cost savings vs accuracy benefits for specialized pretraining.
paper_title: A family of large language models for materials research with insights into model adaptability in continued pretraining
paper_authors: Dhruv Ahlawat, Vaibhav Mishra, Somaditya Singh, Mohd Zaki, Vaibhav Bihani
